class.name: CSGHeightMap3D
class.brief_description: A closed, stepped CSG solid generated from a height map texture.
class.description: Generates one closed CSG solid from [member height_map]. [constant GENERATION_CONTOUR_LAYERS] builds cumulative height contours, extrudes vertical slabs between adjacent quantized levels with a tiny robust Boolean overlap at their joins, and performs one batched union instead of generating geometry per pixel. [constant GENERATION_CELL_GRID] is retained as a detailed fallback and comparison mode. The resulting geometry participates in the regular CSG Boolean, bevel, topology, and modifier pipeline. Faces are tagged with [code]HEIGHTMAP_TOP[/code], [code]HEIGHTMAP_CLIFF[/code], [code]HEIGHTMAP_BORDER[/code], or [code]HEIGHTMAP_BOTTOM[/code] semantics. Surface IDs 0 through 3 represent the same categories. In contour mode, [member slope_width] shifts the upper boundary of each height step toward the solid. This creates inexpensive sloped cliffs without running the general-purpose bevel operation. Use [member layer_settings] to give individual quantized layers different relative heights and slope widths. Array index 0 is layer 0, index 1 is layer 1, and so on. Layer IDs are retained as face metadata through Boolean operations and can be written to a shader custom channel with [constant CSGModifierValue.SOURCE_LAYER_ID]. Enable [member region_enabled] and set [member region_rect] to generate only a pixel region of a large source texture. This allows multiple nodes to share one height map while each builds a small chunk. [b]Note:[/b] Large regions can still produce many top triangles. Increase [member sampling_step] or use [member height_steps] to reduce detail while editing.

members.member: Minimum distance between the bottom and a zero-valued top cell. A positive value prevents degenerate zero-volume cells.
Material used by the bottom. Falls back to [member side_material], then [member material].
Geometry generation strategy. Contour layers are generally much faster for quantized height maps with large same-height regions.
Texture whose sampled values define cell heights.
Number of quantized height levels. Values of 0 and 1 disable quantization.
If [code]true[/code], uses one minus the sampled height.

Optional per-layer overrides. The array index is the stable layer ID. Missing or empty entries use a height weight of 1 and inherit [member slope_width]. Per-layer height weights apply when [member height_steps] is greater than 1.
Material used by top cells and as the fallback for other faces.
If [code]true[/code], only the part of [member height_map] inside [member region_rect] is sampled.

Pixel region sampled when [member region_enabled] is [code]true[/code]. The rectangle is clipped to the texture bounds. [member size] and generated UV coordinates cover the effective region, not the full source texture.
Number of source texels skipped per generated cell. Higher values reduce geometry density.
Material used by height cliffs and outer border walls. Falls back to [member material].

Horizontal inset applied to the upper contour of each height step in [constant GENERATION_CONTOUR_LAYERS]. Outer contours move inward and hole contours move toward the surrounding solid. Chunk-border vertices remain fixed to avoid cracks between adjacent regions. If the requested inset would collapse or split a contour, the largest valid width is selected automatically. This property has no effect in [constant GENERATION_CELL_GRID].
Width, maximum height range, and depth of the generated solid.

constants.constant: Uses perceptual luminance computed from RGB.
Builds a conforming top grid and visible walls directly from sampled cells.
Traces cumulative masks for unique height levels, extrudes non-overlapping slabs between adjacent levels, then combines and simplifies them.
